chunks: From him, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever lends a man silver (dirhams) should not stipulate except that he gets the same amount back; if he is given something better than it, he may accept it, and let none of you take the riding fee of an animal or the loan of goods as a condition for the loan of his silver."
ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for lending money and goods in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir clarifies the mechanics of Qard al-Hasan (benevolent loan) by distinguishing between a stipulated condition (which constitutes riba) and a voluntary gift (hibah). It specifically prohibits 'shart al-istifadah' (conditioning benefit), such as requiring the borrower to rent a mount or use goods, ensuring the loan remains free from hidden interest. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for validating interest-free lending practices while preventing exploitation through indirect benefits.
